capture.final_message:
Treat each side of the two equivalences as an independent standard theorem; there is no mathematical dependency between the unrelated statements paired by `Iff`. After proving all four assertions, assemble each equivalence by ignoring its hypothesis in either direction, then form the conjunction.

The useful intermediate goals are:

1. From `MemLp f p μ`, with `p ≠ 0, ∞` and `ε ≠ 0`, apply the \(L^p\) Chebyshev/Markov inequality to show
   \[
   \mu\{x:\varepsilon\le \|f(x)\|\}<\infty.
   \]
   The nonzero assumptions on \(p\) and \(\varepsilon\), and finiteness of \(p\), are essential here.

2. Use the defining recurrence of the integer-indexed Chebyshev polynomial \(S_n\):
   \[
   S_n=X S_{n-1}-S_{n-2}.
   \]

3. Establish the value of \(U_n\) at zero from its recurrence (or the existing evaluation lemma):
   \[
   U_n(0)=
   \begin{cases}
   (-1)^{n/2},& n\ \text{even},\\
   0,& n\ \text{odd}.
   \end{cases}
   \]
   Use the integer-indexed formulation directly so negative indices are handled correctly.

4. For the extrema statement, use
   \[
   T_n(\cos\theta)=\cos(n\theta)
   \quad\text{and}\quad
   T_n'=n\,U_{n-1}.
   \]
   The roots of \(U_{n-1}\) are exactly \(\cos(k\pi/n)\) for \(0<k<n\). Show these critical points are local extrema via the cosine representation, and rule out all other points because the derivative is nonzero. The hypothesis \(n\ge2\) ensures precisely the stated interior critical points.
